## Historical audit — S0007, chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_104864364/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; offsets are half-open character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal: student request, line 1 [0,11558) | Reconstruct an indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint and appearance. The intended semantic scene is the student’s **classroom interpretation**, not an independently inspected image. |
| First build: student response line 3 [0,12955); execute line 4 [0,13619) | Code specifies room architecture, openings, stage and boards, 21 desk/bench groups, bags, books, fans and fixtures. Named child parts include legs, straps and fan blades; hierarchy and coordinates do not prove physical connection or visual correctness. Colored materials, procedural noise, camera, world and area lights are configured. Some bags and a shutter have explicit rotations; correct pose remains unverified. |
| First validation: execution_result line 5 [0,81551); select line 6 [0,58) | Step 1 reports `ok: true`, a saved render and scene, in 39.84 seconds. This is technical render success, not independent image or geometry verification. |
| Autonomous revision: model_request line 7 [0,106664); student response line 9 [0,13413) | The student received the reference and first render for comparison. Its own comments diagnose a pale image, small/low stage, overly central left desk and shared board/ceiling vertical error. These are student claims, not independently verified findings. It revised camera pitch and lens, stage width, desk and bag placement, bag shape, colors, light powers and exposure. |
| Second validation: execute line 10 [0,14077); execution_result line 11 [0,82297); select line 12 [0,59) | The revised complete program ran, reported `ok: true`, saved a second image and scene in 42.34 seconds, and was selected. No visual comparison of that image is visible in this chunk. |
| Teacher input and exploration: lines 1–12 | No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-message receipt is visible. The student’s comparison and revision are its own; adoption of teacher feedback is therefore not established. The two recorded student sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 8); the two runner executions are visible. |

**Outcome:** Two formally successful executions and a selected second build; final reconstruction quality and overall task outcome are **unknown**. This is neither an empty patch nor an observed technical interruption or algorithm failure. Multiple objects and their intended materials are evidenced by code, but their rendered visibility, relative placement, part contact, poses, texture fidelity, camera framing and lighting quality are not independently established without the images. The student’s camera diagnosis remains a hypothesis, especially because camera and local geometry were changed together.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable distinction is between a successful render and a verified match; editable child parts and an inventory support comparison but do not prove completeness. The particular classroom layout, palette and adjustments are task-specific. Chunk 2 is not visible, so later review, feedback, submission or outcome cannot be inferred.
